# bugs #4159: Error 141 for an identifier after a struct or union tag when a typedef of that name is visible

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4159/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close if the two changed diagnostics for invalid code are acceptable. Related has the enum form, which is not fixed.
- Patch: [bugs-4159.patch](../../patches/bugs-4159.patch), commit [`a7e476c28`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/a7e476c2817b673ba23ef882cebc1a7e99fef841). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

When `typedef struct s s_t;` is written twice, the second line gets error 141, two or more data
types in declaration. C11 6.7 paragraph 3 allows a second typedef of a name for the same type. The
attached `main.c` has the two lines, and on r17193 they get the error for mcs51 with the small and
the large model. The front end reports the error, so it does not depend on the port.

The fault has a second form that the ticket does not name. `struct s t;` in the scope of a typedef
named `t` gets error 141 when it declares an object, a parameter, or a member.

## Cause

The action of `struct_or_union` in `src/SDCC.y` sets `ignoreTypedefType`, so that `check_type` in
`src/SDCC.lex` returns the tag as an identifier when a typedef of that name is visible. The action
of `stag` clears the flag. The parser reads the token after the tag before it reduces the
specifier, because that token decides between a specifier with a member list and one without.
`check_type` therefore returns `TYPE_NAME` for an identifier after the tag when a typedef of that
name is visible, and `mergeSpec` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` reports error 141 for two type specifiers.

After the specifier is reduced, the action of `type_specifier` sets the flag, as the actions for
`char` and the other type specifiers set it. The fault is limited to the one token that the parser
reads before that.

## Fix

With the patch the action of `stag` sets the flag. The lexer clears the flag at each `{` and `(`,
so it reads the type names in a member list as type names. The actions that end a declaration, a
parameter declaration, a member declaration, and a type name clear it with and without the patch.

## Decision

The patch changes two diagnostics for invalid code, and both forms stay errors. A second typedef
that gives the name another struct type gets error 141 without the patch, and error 0 (Duplicate
symbol) and error 51 with it. `struct s t x;` in the scope of a typedef named `t` gets error 141
without the patch and, by the grammar, a syntax error with it. The choice is whether these
messages are acceptable for the two forms. The patch does not have code that keeps error 141 for
them.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4159.c` has 3 functions with 9 assertions. It has second typedefs
of a struct tag, of a union tag, of a struct with a member list, and of a const struct. It has
objects and members that have the names of typedefs, and members of those typedef types after
them. On r17193 the test does not compile for mcs51-small and mcs51-large, the two variants that
were run. With the patch it passes on host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80.

`support/valdiag/tests/bug-4159.c` has 4 cases. The second typedefs must compile. A second typedef
for another struct type, a second typedef with `--std-sdcc99`, and `struct s t x;` must get an
error.

For mcs51-small and mcs51-large, the code size and the tick count of every other regression test
are equal with and without the patch. With the series of this report up to this patch applied to
r17193, the regression suite has 0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80. The
diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

## Related

The enum form of the fault is present on r17193 and with the patch.

- `typedef enum e { A } e_t; typedef enum e e_t;` gets error 141.
- `enum e t;` in the scope of a typedef named `t` gets error 141.
- `typedef enum foo { A } foo; enum foo x;` gets a syntax error.

The rules of `enum_specifier` do not set `ignoreTypedefType` after `enum`. A fix has to clear the
flag at the `:` of an enum type specifier, because a type name follows it.
